## 2. FOSS / Open-Weight LMs & Tools

**DeepSeek V4 preview released**

- **Date:** 2026-04-24  
- **Link:** [MIT Technology Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/04/24/1136422/why-deepseeks-v4-matters/)  
- **Summary:** DeepSeek released a preview of V4, its new flagship open-source model. Reported significance is longer-context handling via a design aimed at processing larger prompts more efficiently.  
- **Why it matters:** Keeps pressure on closed frontier labs by extending open-model capability in long-context workloads, a key surface for coding, research, and enterprise document use.

## 3. Major Financial AI Company News

**Cohere moving to take over Aleph Alpha**

- **Date:** 2026-04-25  
- **Link:** [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/25/why-cohere-is-merging-with-aleph-alpha/)  
- **Summary:** Cohere is reportedly taking over Germany’s Aleph Alpha with Schwarz Group backing, including about €500M in structured financing, to form a Canadian-German sovereign-AI provider for governments and regulated industries.  
- **Why it matters:** The deal shows sovereign AI consolidating around enterprise distribution, national/regional trust requirements, and regulated-sector procurement.

**ComfyUI raises $30M**

- **Date:** 2026-04-24  
- **Link:** [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/24/comfyui-hits-500m-valuation-as-creators-seek-more-control-over-ai-generated-media/)  
- **Summary:** ComfyUI raised $30M at a reported $500M valuation, led by Craft Ventures. The company builds open-source node-based workflows for AI image, video, and audio generation.  
- **Why it matters:** Investor capital is moving into workflow/control layers around generative models, not just the models themselves.

**X-energy raises $1B in IPO**

- **Date:** 2026-04-24  
- **Link:** [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/24/nuclear-startup-x-energy-raises-1b-in-data-center-driven-ipo/)  
- **Summary:** Nuclear startup X-energy raised $1B in an IPO, with demand partly tied to future data-center power needs and an Amazon-linked plan for up to 5 GW of nuclear capacity by 2039.  
- **Why it matters:** AI infrastructure demand is now directly shaping energy-market financing, including long-horizon nuclear bets.

## 4. Major AI Data Center News

**Meta signs AWS Graviton CPU deal**

- **Date:** 2026-04-24  
- **Link:** [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/24/in-another-wild-turn-for-ai-chips-meta-signs-deal-for-millions-of-amazon-ai-cpus/)  
- **Summary:** Meta signed a deal to use millions of Amazon Graviton CPUs for AI workloads.  
- **Why it matters:** Reinforces a shift toward heterogeneous AI infrastructure, with CPUs used alongside GPUs for inference-heavy and agentic workloads.

**Data centers pair batteries with fossil generation**

- **Date:** 2026-04-24  
- **Link:** [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-04-24/data-centers-pair-batteries-and-natural-gas-to-get-power-faster)  
- **Summary:** Bloomberg reported AI data-center operators are pairing batteries with on-site fossil generation to bring power online faster; BloombergNEF tracked 4.9 GW of announced storage co-located with fossil generation at data centers.  
- **Why it matters:** Power availability remains a binding AI scaling constraint, pushing operators toward faster but more carbon-intensive grid-adjacent buildouts.

## 5. Regulation & Policy

**Anthropic updates election safeguards**

- **Date:** 2026-04-24  
- **Link:** [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/election-safeguards-update)  
- **Summary:** Anthropic detailed Claude safeguards for the 2026 U.S. midterms and other elections, including political-bias evaluations, election-misuse tests, influence-operation simulations, voter-information banners, and web-search routing for current election queries.  
- **Why it matters:** Establishes a public safety posture for election-related AI use ahead of a major U.S. cycle.

**OpenAI safety failure draws scrutiny after Canadian killings**

- **Date:** 2026-04-25  
- **Link:** [AP News](https://apnews.com/article/dec2adaad3946583519370eede6a99e2)  
- **Summary:** AP reported Sam Altman apologized after OpenAI did not notify law enforcement about a banned ChatGPT account later linked to killings in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia.  
- **Why it matters:** The incident is likely to intensify scrutiny of AI platforms’ escalation duties, law-enforcement reporting thresholds, and safety governance.
